title: Oral Chemical Burn Due to Occupational Exposure to Potassium Hydroxide: An Unusual Case Report.
journal: Special care in dentistry : official publication of the American Association of Hospital Dentists, the Academy of Dentistry for the Handicapped, and the American Society for Geriatric Dentistry
first_affiliation: Department of Oral Diagnosis, Dental School, University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Piracicaba, Piracicaba, São Paulo, Brazil.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To report an uncommon case of oral chemical burn caused by occupational exposure to potassium hydroxide (KOH) managed with photobiomodulation (PBM).

abstract.label: CASE REPORT
abstract.text: A 50-year-old man experienced occupational exposure to KOH while working in a food factory. The accident occurred during maintenance of a pipeline that should have been empty; however, it was still carrying a 50% KOH solution. The patient presented with severe pain and impaired speech, nutrition, and hydration due to the extent of the lesions. Clinical examination revealed diffuse ulcerations affecting the lower labial semimucosa, upper and lower labial mucosa, and dorsal tongue. A clinical diagnosis of KOH-induced chemical burn was established, and daily PBM therapy was initiated using red (660 nm) and infrared (850 nm) light-emitting diodes (LEDs) to provide pain control and promote mucosal repair. Rapid improvement of signs and symptoms was observed throughout treatment, with complete mucosal healing achieved after eight sessions of PBM.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This report describes, to the best of our knowledge, the first documented case of oral burn caused by KOH in an occupational setting, highlighting the severity of alkali-induced lesions and the therapeutic potential of PBM therapy.

title: Comment on "Patient satisfaction with treatments for burning mouth syndrome: A retrospective study using the self-assessment of treatment questionnaire and visual analogue scale".
journal: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery
first_affiliation: Department of Internal Medicine in Family Medicine, Bukhara State Medical Institute named after Abu Ali ibn Sino, Bukhara, Uzbekistan. Electronic address: pureworship2026@outlook.com.

title: Low-level laser therapy in ulcerative lesions in leprosy: a systematic review.
first_affiliation: Universidade Estadual do Oeste do Paraná, Paraná, Brazil.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Leprosy is a disease that affects the peripheral nerves and ulcers are among the main complications of the disease. The laser is a tool with wide use in physiotherapy, with proven efficacy in the improvement of pressure ulcers, which creates the possibility of studies on its action in leprosy lesions. The aim of this study was to review the literature on the efficacy of low-level laser therapy (LLLT) in the healing process of leprosy lesions.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: Articles were sought in databases according to specific search criteria for each database as results of the descriptors included using EndNote Web (Clarivate, UK). The risk of bias (RoB) was analysed using Cochrane's ROBINS-I and RoB2 tools.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 259 studies were included, involving 49 patients. After exclusion of duplicates and following a full reading, three articles remained for inclusion in this review. Of the three studies, only two had positive results for LLLT on the healing of leprosy ulcers; however, no study showed low RoB.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The findings of this review concluded that use of LLLT in the study population was effective in reducing the size of leprosy lesions. Due to the lack of primary studies with low RoB, more primary studies are required to provide stronger evidence on the use of LLLT in the treatment of leprosy ulcers.

title: Integrated Traditional Chinese Medicine, Mili-Fire Needle, and Light-Emitting Diode Phototherapy for Cystic Acne and Post-Acne Sequelae.
first_affiliation: Department of Dermatology, The Fifth People's Hospital of Changshu.

abstract.text: Moderate-to-severe cystic acne is difficult to manage because active inflammatory lesions often coexist with a risk of persistent erythema, scarring, and acne-related quality-of-life impairment. This study evaluated an integrated traditional Chinese medicine regimen combined with mili-fire needle therapy and light-emitting diode red-blue phototherapy for short-term lesion control and post-treatment sequelae outcomes. Sixty patients with moderate-to-severe cystic acne were enrolled in a single-center, parallel-group clinical study and randomly assigned to a control group or treatment group. The control group received oral isotretinoin and red-blue light irradiation, while the treatment group received modified Zhibai Dihuang Wan combined with Erzhi Wan, mili-fire needle therapy, and the same red-blue light irradiation. Both groups used topical adapalene and received identical skin-care and lifestyle guidance. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, after three treatment courses, and after six treatment courses. A post-treatment responder follow-up cohort included only patients who achieved cure or marked improvement and therefore did not preserve the original randomized comparison. Both regimens reduced Global Acne Grading System scores, lesion counts, and Acne Disability Index scores; between-group values favored the integrated-regimen group after three and six courses. The cure-plus-marked-response proportions were 46.67% in the control group and 76.67% in the treatment group; the ordinal clinical-response distribution differed between groups, whereas adverse-event rates did not differ significantly. In the selected responder cohort, the treatment group had lower acne scar, Vancouver Scar Scale, and imaging-based erythema scores during months 1-3. The randomized short-term findings support further evaluation of the integrated regimen, while the responder-only follow-up findings should be considered exploratory and require confirmation in studies that follow the full randomized cohort.

title: Can Photobiomodulation improve healing of category II-III pressure ulcers in frail older adults? A quasi-experimental 24-month follow-up study.
first_affiliation: Department of Nursing, Umeå University, Umeå, Västerbotten, Sweden.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Frail older adults are particularly susceptible to pressure ulcer development due to complex health conditions and functional decline. Pressure ulcers category II and III involve partial- and full-thickness skin loss, and current treatment options often yield suboptimal outcomes. The study evaluated the effects of adjunctive photobiomodulation compared with standard-of-care in frail older adults, with category II and III pressure ulcers. The objectives were to assess: 1) ulcer healing 2) healing time; 3) factors associated with healing, and 4) ulcer recurrence following photobiomodulation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Quasi-experimental study with two prospective intervention groups and matched registry-based control groups, conducted in accordance with TREND guidelines. Baseline differences analysed using Independent Samples T-test, Independent Samples Mann-Whitney U test or Pearson chi-square test. Times to healing evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and log-rank tests. Age-stratified multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were applied to identify healing-associated factors. Ulcer recurrences were analysed descriptively.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING
abstract.text: Intervention groups comprised frail older adults (≥70 years) receiving municipal home healthcare: category II (n = 39) and category III (n = 37). Photobiomodulation was administered twice weekly, using GaAs laser (904 nm) and AlGaInP laser (635 nm). Control groups treated with standard-of-care were identified from the Swedish national registry RiksSår for ulcer treatment: category II (n = 117), and category III (n = 111).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The photobiomodulation groups demonstrated higher proportions of healed ulcers and significantly shorter healing times (p < 0.001). Median healing times were 33 and 70 days for the category II and III ulcers, respectively, compared with 153 and 195 days in the control groups. Ulcer recurrence within 24 months following photobiomodulation was 0% for category II and 6,7% for category III.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Photobiomodulation may be an effective treatment for pressure ulcers in frail older adults, substantially accelerating healing, and reducing recurrence, with potential to lessen patient burden and improve outcomes.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07520825.

title: Red and near-infrared photobiomodulation in precision medicine: mechanisms, dosimetry, and clinical translation.
first_affiliation: Medical Equipment Department, Affiliated Hospital of Jining Medical University, Jining, Shandong, China.

abstract.text: Phototherapy is a non-invasive therapeutic modality that uses specific wavelengths of light to modulate biological processes and treat disease. Driven by advances in photobiology, regenerative medicine, and clinical technology, phototherapy has evolved from empirical heliotherapy into a mechanism-based intervention with expanding medical applications. This review places the biological effects, therapeutic indications, and safety profiles of ultraviolet, blue, and green light in comparative context, while focusing primarily on the mechanisms, dosimetry, and clinical translation of red and near-infrared photobiomodulation (PBM). Although ultraviolet and blue light therapies have established roles in dermatology and neonatal jaundice, their clinical use is limited by concerns such as photocarcinogenesis, retinal phototoxicity, and circadian disruption. In contrast, red and near-infrared light offer deeper tissue penetration and, when appropriately dosed, a comparatively low risk of direct photochemical injury. Through mitochondrial, redox, inflammatory, and other context-dependent signaling pathways, red/NIR PBM has been investigated in wound repair, chronic pain, osteoarthritis, musculoskeletal disorders, neurological conditions, and dermatological applications. As a representative quantitative example, a 2024 meta-analysis of 10 placebo-controlled randomized trials involving 542 participants with knee osteoarthritis found a moderate reduction in pain at rest with PBM compared with placebo (standardized mean difference, - 0.70; 95% confidence interval, - 1.10 to - 0.20), although the certainty of evidence was very low. However, broader clinical translation remains constrained by heterogeneous dosimetry, insufficiently standardized treatment protocols, and uneven evidence maturity across indications. To address these limitations, we propose a precision-oriented framework that links clinical target, tissue-optical context, wavelength selection, patient- and site-specific modifiers, dosimetric implications, measurable endpoints, and evidence maturity. This framework is intended to support treatment planning, parameter reporting, and prospective validation rather than to prescribe currently validated individualized dosing algorithms.

title: Anti-Aging Efficacy of a Home-use red and Infrared Light-Emitting Diode Mask and a Cream: Ex Vivo and Clinical Evaluations in Women With Mature Skin.
journal: Skin research and technology : official journal of International Society for Bioengineering and the Skin (ISBS) [and] International Society for Digital Imaging of Skin (ISDIS) [and] International Society for Skin Imaging (ISSI)
first_affiliation: Laboratoires, Pontoise, France.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Photobiomodulation has gained considerable attention for its potential in various dermatological applications. We assessed the anti-aging effects of a home-use face-fit mask combining 630 and 850 nm light-emitting diodes (LEDs) and an anti-aging cream in ex vivo and prospective exploratory clinical studies. Both products are commercially available.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Skin samples from six women aged 39─55 years were either left untreated or received topical treatments for 7 days: LED irradiation (7-minute sessions) or cream (2 mg/cm2), or both. In the clinical study, women aged 49─65 years (n = 50) applied the cream daily to the face and neck for 56 days and used the mask 3─4 times per week.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Compared to untreated skin samples, the combination of LEDs and cream increased the expression of elastin (+29.6%) and collagen 1 (+7.6%) (p< 0.05 for both). The expression of elastin also increased following treatment with the LEDs alone (+26.1%; p< 0.05). the effect of LEDs and cream combined treatment was demonstrated on collagen 1 expression, with a similar trend observed for elastin expression. In the clinical study, investigator-assessed clinical scores showed significant progressive improvements from baseline, reaching +57.1% for skin radiance, -39.4% for pore dilatation, and -24.2% for crow's feet wrinkle depth at Day 56 (p< 0.0001 for all). Participants also perceived significantly improved skin radiance and smoothing of face and neck wrinkles throughout the study.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The LED mask and the anti-aging cream led to visible and clinically measurable skin signs of ageing reduction versus baseline. The increase in collagen I and elastin expression observed in the ex vivo study could contribute to the visible reduction in signs of aging demonstrated in the clinical study.

title: Adjuvant 904 nm Gallium Arsenide Laser Therapy Enhances Healing and Reduces Bacterial Burden in Chronic Wounds: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Wound repair and regeneration : official publication of the Wound Healing Society [and] the European Tissue Repair Society
first_affiliation: Programa de Pós-Graduação Em Ciências da Saúde, Universidade Federal dos Vales do Jequitinhonha e Mucuri, Diamantina, Minas Gerais, Brazil.

abstract.text: Chronic wounds, characterized by prolonged healing times and high complication rates, present significant challenges to healthcare systems. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial evaluated the adjunctive effect of 904 nm gallium arsenide (GaAs) laser therapy in the treatment of chronic venous and diabetic ulcers. The study adhered to the CONSORT 2025 guidelines to ensure transparency and quality in reporting. Seventy patients were randomly assigned to two groups: active laser (AL) group (laser + standard care) and placebo laser group (PL) (simulated laser + standard care). All participants were followed twice a week until complete wound healing or a maximum of 15 sessions. Outcomes assessed included wound area reduction, microbial load and histological analysis. Results showed that the AL group had a 53% reduction in wound area, while the PL group had a 9% reduction (p < 0.001), with complete closure observed in two AL patients. Laser therapy also significantly reduced bacterial colonization, particularly, of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli and Proteus mirabilis (p ≤ 0.007). Histological analysis demonstrated enhanced angiogenesis, reduced inflammatory infiltrate and improved collagen organization at the wound edges in the AL group (p ≤ 0.042). These findings demonstrate that 904 nm GaAs laser therapy accelerates healing, reduces microbial burden and promotes favourable tissue remodelling. The integrative approach, combining clinical, microbiological and histological assessments, underscores its potential as a safe and effective adjunct in chronic wound management, offering a promising strategy to improve outcomes and reduce healthcare burdens.

title: Fractional CO₂ laser combined with intradermal and topical platelet-rich plasma for hypertrophic scars: a randomized controlled trial.
first_affiliation: Geriatric Hospital Affiliated to Wuhan University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: This study compared the clinical efficacy and safety of fractional CO₂ laser combined with platelet-rich plasma (PRP) delivered by intradermal injection plus topical application versus fractional CO₂ laser alone for the treatment of hypertrophic scars.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective, randomized, assessor-blinded trial, 120 patients were assigned to a combined group (laser + PRP, n = 60) or a control group (laser + saline, n = 60). Four sessions were delivered at 4-6-week intervals. The primary outcome was Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS) total score. The prespecified primary endpoint was the between-group difference in VSS total score at T4 (6 months after the final treatment session). Secondary outcomes included POSAS scores, ultrasound-measured scar thickness, patient satisfaction, and adverse events.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Both groups showed significant VSS improvement (both P < 0.001). The combined group had significantly lower VSS total scores than the control group from T1 onward (P = 0.036 at T1; P < 0.001 at T2 and T4; P = 0.007 at T3; estimated between-group difference at T4 -1.85 points, 95% CI -2.48 to -1.22, from the primary mixed-effects model) and lower POSAS scores from T1 onward (P = 0.022 at T1; P < 0.001 at T2, T3, and T4) than the control group. Ultrasound-measured scar thickness was lower in the combined group at 3 months (P = 0.045); at 6 months the difference was attenuated and of borderline statistical significance (P = 0.042-0.065 across missing-data approaches). Patient satisfaction was higher in the combined group (P < 0.001). Procedural pain was greater in the combined group (mean between-group difference 1.34 points on a 0-10 VAS; P < 0.001). Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation was numerically lower in the combined group (18.33% vs. 33.33%; P = 0.094).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Fractional CO₂ laser combined with intradermal and topical PRP provided greater improvement in clinical scar scores than laser alone, with an acceptable safety profile. The advantage in ultrasound-measured thickness at 6 months was of borderline statistical significance. These findings support PRP as a potential adjunct for hypertrophic scars.

title: Thermographic outcomes of auricular laser acupuncture and auricular seed acupressure in older adults with chronic shoulder pain: an exploratory nonrandomized, nonconcurrent comparison.
first_affiliation: Postgraduate Program in Biomedical Engineering, Universidade do Vale do Paraíba (UNIVAP), São José dos Campos, Brazil. gersonquadros@yahoo.com.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Compare pain, quality of life, and cutaneous temperature changes within predefined anterior, lateral, and posterior shoulder regions of interest between auricular laser acupuncture and seed acupressure in older adults with chronic shoulder pain.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This exploratory, nonrandomized, open-label study enrolled 20 adults aged 60-90 years, allocated by order of entry to consecutive, nonconcurrent cohorts of auricular laser acupuncture (n = 10) or seed acupressure (n = 10), treated twice weekly for five weeks. VAS, McGill, SF-36, and thermography were assessed before the first (A1) and fifth sessions (A2) and after the tenth (A3) and analyzed using linear mixed-effects models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From A1 to A3, VAS decreased by - 2.70 points in Laser (95% CI - 4.37 to - 1.03) and - 2.50 in Seed (95% CI - 4.17 to - 0.83); the between-group difference was - 0.20 points (Laser - Seed; 95% CI - 2.54 to 2.14). Selected McGill and SF-36 outcomes changed; McGill affective A1-to-A2 change differed between groups (Laser - Seed: -2.70; 95% CI - 4.86 to - 0.55; p = 0.017). Anterior thermal range (ΔT) showed a TIME × GROUP interaction (p = 0.007); the A1-to-A3 between-group difference was - 1.941 °C (Seed - Laser; 95% CI - 3.097 to - 0.785), although Seed ΔT was higher at baseline (+ 1.496 °C; 95% CI 0.607 to 2.385). Lateral ΔT showed a TIME effect (p = 0.033); posterior ΔT showed none.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Clinical outcomes improved over time without evidence of differential changes between interventions. Thermography identified region-specific ΔT trajectories, warranting further investigation as a complementary method.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07010627.

title: Laser as an Adjunct in Endodontic Treatment in Dogs: Perspectives on a Conservative, Effective, and Safe Approach.
first_affiliation: Faculty of Veterinary Medicine and Animal Science, University of São Paulo, São Paulo, Brazil.

abstract.text: Crown fractures and subsequent pulp necrosis are common clinical findings in veterinary dental practice. While conventional endodontic therapy typically yields favorable outcomes, light therapies, such as antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) and photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT), have emerged as promising adjuncts for enhancing disinfection and tissue repair. However, standardized protocols for these therapies in veterinary dentistry remain scarce. This clinical case report describes the management of a maxillary incisor with pulp necrosis secondary to a coronal fracture in a dog. Following conventional chemomechanical preparation, aPDT was performed using 0.01% methylene blue as a photosensitizer and a 660 nm diode laser (100 mW, 9 J) delivered via an intracanal diffusing fiber. Immediately after the endodontic canal manipulation, the diode laser (PBMT; 808 nm, 3 J/point) was applied using contact transmucosal mode to modulate inflammation and stimulate periapical bone repair, followed by weekly sessions for 3 weeks. Radiographic and clinical follow-up at day 1, 2 and 8 weeks, and 1 year postoperatively demonstrated progressive alveolar healing and the absence of clinical symptoms. The combined use of aPDT and PBMT with the described laser parameters seemed to be a promising, conservative and effective approach to optimize root canal disinfection, promoting local analgesy and possible accelerating apical bone remodeling. The results suggest that light therapies are valuable tools for enhancing endodontic success in dogs.

title: Treatment of pyogenic granuloma with a 577-nm diode laser in dark-skinned patients: A prospective case series.
first_affiliation: Department of Dermatology, Al-Azhar University, Asyut, Egypt. dessam73@azhar.edu.eg.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Pyogenic granulomas are common benign vascular lesions found on exposed skin in children. Treatment in darker skin types can be challenging because of increased epidermal melanin absorption and the associated risk of collateral thermal injury.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a 577-nm diode laser for the treatment of pyogenic granuloma in patients with dark skin types.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Nine patients with pyogenic granuloma and skin types IV-V were enrolled in this prospective case series. They were treated every two weeks with a 577 nm diode laser using a 1 mm spot size, with fluence ranging from 19-23 J/cm2 depending on lesion size until bleeding stopped. Sessions were repeated every two weeks until complete clearance. Patients were followed clinically and photographically every two weeks, and then one month after the final session.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: This prospective case series included 9 patients clinically diagnosed with pyogenic granuloma. The mean age was 18.0 ± 14.6 years (range, 6-40 years), and the mean duration of pyogenic granuloma was 9.1 ± 3.94 months. Lesions were present on the lips of 4 patients (44.4%), the cheeks in 2 patients (22.2%), hands (2 patients, 22.2%), and neck (1 patient, 11.1%). All patients were treated with a 577 nm diode laser session every 2 weeks until complete clearance. Complete clearance was achieved in 3 patients after the first session, 4 patients after the second session, 1 patient after third session, and only one patient required four treatment sessions. Atrophic scarring was the only reported side effect, occurring in one case.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Treatment with a 577-nm diode laser appears to be a safe and effective option for pyogenic granuloma in patients with darker skin types.

title: Comparative evaluation of hyaluronic acid spray and low-level laser therapy on wound healing following gingivectomy: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
first_affiliation: Akdeniz University, Antalya, Turkey. narzu@hotmail.com.

abstract.text: Gingivectomy wounds heal by secondary intention, prolonging recovery and postoperative discomfort; this randomized controlled trial compared low-level laser therapy and hyaluronic acid spray for early wound healing and postoperative pain after gingivectomy. Systemically healthy patients requiring gingivectomy were randomly allocated to receive either LLLT (940 nm diode laser, 3 W, 128.4 J/cm2, applied on days 0, 3, 5, and 7) or 0.04% high-molecular-weight HA spray (applied twice daily for 7 days). Wound epithelialization was quantified through Mira-2-Ton plaque-disclosing staining combined with digital planimetric analysis (ImageJ) at baseline and on postoperative days 3, 7, and 14. Secondary outcomes included gingival index (GI), full-mouth bleeding score (FMBS), probing pocket depth (PPD), and visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores. A total of 64 participants were enrolled and randomized (n = 32 per group). Both groups exhibited significant wound area reduction over time (p < 0.001). However, the HA spray group demonstrated significantly higher wound epithelialization percentages (percentage reduction from baseline in the non-epithelialized, disclosing-solution-stained wound surface area) than the LLLT group on days 3 (p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.39), 7 (p < 0.001; d = 1.12), and 14 (p = 0.044; d = 0.73). The HA spray group also reported significantly lower VAS pain scores on days 1 and 3 (p < 0.05). Periodontal parameters improved significantly from baseline to week 6 in both groups (all p < 0.001), with no significant between-group differences at week 6 for GI (p = 0.999), FMBS (p = 0.843), or PPD (p = 0.718). HA spray yielded significantly accelerated re-epithelialization and superior early pain reduction compared to LLLT following gingivectomy, suggesting it may serve as a practical, patient-friendly adjunctive alternative to laser biostimulation in postoperative wound management. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Number: NCT07034625.

title: Re: The efficacy, satisfaction, and safety of carbon dioxide (CO2) fractional laser in combination with pulsed dye laser (PDL) versus each one alone in the treatment of hypertrophic burn scars: a single-blinded randomized controlled trial.
first_affiliation: Third Affiliated Hospital of Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, Beijing, China.

abstract.text: This letter comments on the randomized trial by Karimi Kivi et al. comparing pulsed dye laser (PDL), ablative fractional carbon dioxide laser (AFCL), and their combination for hypertrophic burn scars. Several reporting and methodological issues warrant clarification, including the apparent inconsistency in the presentation of Vancouver Scar Scale data, the discrepancy between the reported total number of scars and the numbers shown in the original article, and the statistical handling of multiple scars from the same patient. Clarification of these issues would improve the transparency and interpretability of the study and facilitate its appropriate use in future evidence syntheses.

title: Histological effects of chitosan, chitosan-carried hyaluronic acid, and photobiomodulation on palatal wound healing in rats: an in vivo study.
first_affiliation: Department of Periodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, Tehran Medical Sciences, Islamic Azad University, 19395-1495, Tehran, Iran.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To compare the histological effects of topical chitosan (CS), a hyaluronic acid-chitosan gel (HA/CS), and photobiomodulation (PBM) on palatal wound healing in rats.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Sixty male Wistar rats were randomized to control, CS, HA/CS, or PBM groups (n = 15/group). Standardized 5-mm full-thickness palatal wounds were created. Gels were applied three times daily; PBM (660 nm, 150 mW, 4.2 J/cm², 14 s) was administered on days 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, and 13. Five independent animals/group were assessed on days 3, 7, and 14. The animal was the experimental unit, and re-epithelialization was the prespecified primary outcome. Ordinal scores were compared at each endpoint using Kruskal-Wallis and Bonferroni-adjusted Dunn tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: HA/CS had higher re-epithelialization scores than control on days 3 (adjusted p = 0.003) and 7 (adjusted p = 0.024), and than PBM on day 3 (adjusted p = 0.015). PBM exceeded control on day 7 (adjusted p = 0.024). All day-14 animals had the maximum epithelial score. HA/CS had higher fibroblast scores than control on day 3; all interventions had higher fibroblast and angiogenesis scores than control on days 7 and 14. Collagen scores exceeded control with CS and HA/CS on day 3 and HA/CS on days 7 and 14.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The tested HA/CS formulation showed favorable early epithelial and selected stromal findings. Day-14 epithelial scores showed a ceiling effect. HA-specific effects and HA-CS synergy cannot be established.

title: Umbrella review of low-level light therapy: evidence across clinical conditions.
first_affiliation: Global Cooperation Center, Korea Institute of Oriental Medicine, Daejeon, Korea, Republic of.

abstract.text: Low-level light therapy (LLLT) and photobiomodulation (PBM) have been studied in diverse clinical fields. Although numerous systematic reviews have been published, their findings are fragmented and inconsistent. This umbrella review of systematic reviews aimed to synthesize the evidence on the effectiveness and safety of LLLT across various clinical conditions. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science databases were searched from inception to February 24, 2026. Eligible studies were systematic reviews or meta-analyses of LLLT in humans. Data on clinical conditions, intervention characteristics, overall direction of conclusions, and adverse events were extracted. Methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2. A total of 100 systematic reviews were included, representing 1,164 primary-study occurrences and 790 unique eligible primary studies. Oral and dental conditions accounted for the largest evidence base (53 reviews), followed by musculoskeletal disorders (22 reviews), oncology-related complications (8 reviews), and wound and lymphatic conditions (8 reviews). Overall, 62 reviews reached conclusions favoring the evaluated intervention, 34 reported neutral or mixed conclusions, and 4 had unclear conclusions. The highest proportion of favorable conclusions was observed for oncology-related complications. Of the 100 reviews, 11 reported one or more adverse events or side effects, 32 explicitly reported no adverse events, and 57 did not provide adverse-event information. Most reviews received low (30.0%) or critically low (60.0%) overall confidence ratings using AMSTAR 2. The review literature suggests potential clinical benefit of LLLT in selected indications, particularly oncology-related complications such as oral mucositis. However, these descriptive patterns do not establish treatment efficacy or the certainty of the underlying evidence. Heterogeneity in treatment parameters, generally low methodological confidence, and incomplete adverse-event reporting limit interpretation and preclude firm conclusions about safety.

title: Transcranial photobiomodulation reduces predator-induced anxiety-like behavior (risk assessment) in male Rattus norvegicus threatened by Bothrops jararaca pit vipers.
first_affiliation: Laboratory of Neuroanatomy and Neuropsychobiology, Department of Pharmacology, Ribeirão Preto Medical School of the University of São Paulo (FMRP-USP), Ribeirão Preto, Brazil.

abstract.text: Photobiomodulation, also known as low-level laser therapy, uses specific wavelengths of light to stimulate biological tissues. Evidence from the literature indicates that transcranial photobiomodulation can alter neurophysiological activity; however, studies investigating its effects on the neurobiology of emotions remain scarce. Therefore, the objective of the present study was to investigate the effects of acute transcranial photobiomodulation administered at five irradiation sites using an 808 nm (± 10 nm) wavelength on anxiety-like behavior in rodents (Rattus norvegicus) exposed to either a potential wild predator (Bothrops jararaca) or predator-related cues (snake odor). Both the presence of the snake and exposure to its odor elicited anxiety-like risk-assessment behavior in the rodents. In turn, photobiomodulation treatment significantly reduced both the frequency and duration of this behavior, suggesting a potential anxiolytic-like effect.

title: Photobiomodulation Therapy in Head and Neck Cancer Patients Undergoing Chemoradiotherapy: Role in Toxicities Prevention.
first_affiliation: Department of Radiation Oncology, Institute Gustave Roussy, 94805 Villejuif, France.

abstract.text: Background: Chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for head and neck cancer (HNC) is frequently associated with severe acute toxicities that compromise treatment adherence and quality of life. This study evaluated the effectiveness of photobiomodulation (PBM) in reducing CRT-induced toxicities in a real-world cohort. Methods: Between May 2021 and July 2024, we retrospectively analyzed 117 HNC patients treated with definitive or adjuvant CRT and concomitant PBM: a non-invasive application of red or near-infrared light to cutaneous and mucosal surfaces to modulate inflammatory responses, using 620/820 nm or 650 nm devices, with irradiation times of 2-12 min and energy densities of 3-12 J/cm2 according to the treatment protocol. Toxicities were graded according to CTCAE v 5.0 at baseline, during treatment, at treatment completion, and throughout follow-up. Associations with toxicity were assessed with logistic regression for repeated measurements (generalized estimating equations). Patients were stratified according to PBM exposure (<10 vs. ≥10 sessions). Results: Median follow-up was 16 months. At treatment completion, grade 2-3 oral mucositis and radiodermatitis occurred in 38.5% and 25.6% of patients, respectively, both lower than rates reported in historical cohorts without PBM. Patients receiving ≥10 PBM sessions (72 pts) experienced significantly lower rates of grade 2-3 odynophagia at treatment completion (16.7% vs. 42.2%, p = 0.005) and persistent dysphagia at the last follow-up (12.5% vs. 33.3%, p = 0.009). PBM exposure was not associated with significant differences in weight loss, progression-free survival, or overall survival. Conclusions: This study provides real-world data on toxicity outcomes among HNC patients receiving PBM, with lower rates of selected toxicities observed among patients receiving ≥10 PBM sessions. Although the retrospective design and lack of a control group limit causal inference, these findings provide a strong rationale for prospective randomized trials to define the optimal PBM schedule and validate its clinical impact.

title: Efficacy and Safety of At-Home Light-Emitting Diode Photobiomodulation for Facial Rejuvenation: A Systematic Review.
first_affiliation: Department of Plastic Surgery, Vanderbilt University Medical Center, 1161 21st Ave S, Nashville, TN, United States of America. rishub.das@gmail.com.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Photobiomodulation using light-emitting diode (LED) devices has gained popularity for facial rejuvenation. Evidence supporting the safety and efficacy of at-home devices remains fragmented. We aimed to summarize the existing literature evaluating the clinical effectiveness and safety of at-home LED photobiomodulation devices for facial rejuvenation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic search of MEDLINE/PubMed was conducted for relevant clinical studies, following PRISMA guidelines. Randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort or split-face studies evaluating at-home LED devices for facial rejuvenation were included; studies of in-office devices, laser-based systems, or preclinical models were excluded. Data on wavelength, treatment regimen, clinical outcomes, and adverse events were extracted from each study. Objective and subjective measures of facial aging, including wrinkles, skin elasticity, smoothness, hydration, pore size, and patient-reported cosmetic satisfaction were evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eight studies comprising 365 participants met inclusion criteria. Treatment wavelengths ranged from 440 to 1072 nm, with red and near-infrared light most commonly used. Across studies, at-home LED therapy was associated with statistically significant improvements in multiple clinical features of facial aging, including wrinkles, skin texture, elasticity, and periorbital rhytids, along with high patient satisfaction. Adverse events were infrequent, mild, and transient.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: At-home LED photobiomodulation devices appear to be safe and effective for improving facial aging parameters, particularly those emitting red and near-infrared wavelengths. However, variability in treatment protocols, limited comparative data, and underrepresentation of diverse skin phenotypes highlight the need for larger, standardized, and comparative trials to define their role in evidence-based care.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE I
abstract.text: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

title: Dual-Wavelength Laser Therapy for Painful Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: A Randomized, Double-Blind, and Sham-Controlled Trial.
first_affiliation: Franco & Co-Podiatric Medicine & Surgery, Miramar, Florida, USA.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is common and often inadequately controlled with pharmacological therapy. This study evaluated a clinician-directed, prescription home-use dual-wavelength low-level laser therapy device for temporary relief of painful DPN.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial conducted at four independent U.S. clinical sites, 64 adults with painful DPN were randomized 1:1 to active treatment (n = 33) or sham treatment (n = 31). The active device emitted simultaneous 640 red and 405 nm violet coherent laser light. Participants self-administered treatment twice daily for 3 weeks, with each session consisting of 5 min per foot. The primary endpoint was the proportion of participants achieving at least a 30% reduction in visual analog scale (VAS) foot pain score from baseline to Week 3. Secondary outcomes included VAS change, neuropathic pain symptoms, treatment satisfaction, durability through Week 7, adherence, blinding integrity, and safety. Participants were required to maintain a stable analgesic and neuropathic-pain regimen throughout, so the intervention was delivered in addition to existing standard care. The primary endpoint was analyzed in the intent-to-treat population, with single imputation for the four participants who withdrew before receiving a device.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: At Week 3, 72.7% of active-treated participants met the primary responder criterion compared with 32.3% of sham-treated participants, a between-group difference of 40.5 percentage points (95% CI 18.1 to 62.9) (p = 0.0024). Mean VAS reduction was greater with active treatment than sham treatment (-33.4 vs -20.0 points; p = 0.026). Improvements were sustained through Week 7, with favorable symptom trends, higher satisfaction, and no serious device-related adverse events. Improvement on the neuropathic pain symptom inventory was greatest for paresthesia/dysesthesia, paroxysmal pain, and burning pain and was not evident for evoked pain.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Prescription home-use dual-wavelength laser therapy was well tolerated and produced clinically meaningful short-term reductions in foot pain in adults with painful DPN at four independent clinical sites. Because assessment ended four weeks after treatment completion, the findings support short-term pain relief, and the intervention is best positioned as a complementary, nonpharmacological modality used alongside standard care.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05291975.

title: Angular and Spectral Engineering of Red Organic Light-Emitting Diodes via Cavity-Induced Emission for Photobiomodulation-Related Cellular Responses.
first_affiliation: Department of Physics, Dongguk University, Seoul04620, Republic of Korea.

abstract.text: Photobiomodulation using red and near-infrared light has emerged as a promising strategy for promoting skin regeneration because of its ability to stimulate mitochondrial activity and enhance cellular proliferation. However, the optical characteristics of the light source, including angular emission and spectral bandwidth, remain underexplored in terms of their influence on biological outcomes. Here, we demonstrate that emission-engineered red organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) can directly regulate cellular responses by tailoring both angular distribution and spectral properties. Flexible OLED devices were fabricated with three representative configurations: an indium tin oxide (ITO)-based Lambertian emission device (inflexible), a candle-emission device with a narrow spectral profile centered at 610 nm, and a batwing-emission device exhibiting angularly broadened and spectrally enriched output (610-650 nm). Systematic optical characterization revealed distinct differences in efficiency, full width at half maximum (FWHM), and angular emission patterns across these devices. Subsequent in vitro assays showed that both candle and batwing devices enhanced proliferation-related cellular responses relative to sham-irradiation and ITO controls, with the batwing device producing the strongest effect. The superior biological efficacy of the batwing device is attributed to its broadened multiwavelength emission, providing broader spectral overlap with biologically relevant wavelengths. The implications of these optical characteristics for tissue photobiomodulation are discussed based on previous studies. This work establishes a direct connection between OLED emission characteristics and biological efficacy, underscoring emission control as a key parameter in optimizing photobiomodulation.

title: Physical Rehabilitation for Postpartum Perineal Morbidity After Episiotomy and Childbirth-Related Perineal Trauma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
first_affiliation: Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology College of Medicine, Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Postpartum perineal trauma commonly causes pain and delayed maternal recovery, yet randomized evidence supporting rehabilitation interventions remains fragmented.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare the effectiveness of physical and electrophysical rehabilitation modalities for postpartum perineal pain, wound healing, and oedema following episiotomy or childbirth-related perineal trauma.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, CINAHL, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ICTRP were searched from inception to April 7, 2026. Randomized controlled trials evaluating rehabilitation modalities were included. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed where appropriate, and methodological quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nine randomized controlled trials were included, seven of which contributed to quantitative synthesis. TENS significantly reduced short-term postpartum perineal pain compared with control (SMD -1.19, 95% CI -1.83 to -0.55). LLLT showed no significant benefit (SMD -0.16, 95% CI -0.52 to 0.19), while therapeutic ultrasound demonstrated no significant reduction in persistent pain. Narrative evidence indicated favorable effects of cooling interventions on oedema, immediate pain relief, and maternal satisfaction. Two studies were judged at low risk of bias, five had some concerns, and two were at high risk of bias.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This review provides the first comparative synthesis of randomized evidence evaluating physical and electrophysical rehabilitation modalities for postpartum perineal morbidity. The strongest evidence currently supports TENS for short-term pain relief, whereas cooling interventions appear beneficial for local symptom management. Larger, rigorously designed randomized trials are required to establish evidence-based rehabilitation strategies for postpartum perineal recovery.

title: Comparison of the effects of different dental pulp stem cell preconditioning protocols on the odontogenic potential of their derived small extracellular vesicles.
first_affiliation: Oral Biology Department, Faculty of Dentistry, Mansoura University, Mansoura, Egypt. Dr_rana_nagah@mans.edu.eg.

abstract.text: Regenerative endodontic therapy that is based on the use of stem cells or their derivatives to induce dentin-pulp complex regeneration has recently gained substantial interest. This study aimed to compare the effect of preconditioning through odontogenesis (OD) and/or low-level laser therapy photobiostimulation (LLLT) of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs) on the regenerative potentials of their derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) aiming to develop a novel pulp capping therapy. In the current study, hDPSCs were subjected to OD, LLLT, or dual preconditioning protocols before the isolation of sEVs, then the derived sEVs were co-cultured with naïve hDPSCs. Cell viability and wound healing capacity were evaluated using MTT and scratch assays, respectively. RT-qPCR was performed for odontogenic gene expression (DSPP, DMP1, and COL1A1), followed by immunocytochemical staining. Matrix mineralization was also assessed, and relevant statistical analyses were performed. All sEVs-treated groups revealed enhanced cellular and odontogenic activities. OD-sEVs enhanced wound healing and mineralization, while LLLT-sEVs showed relatively higher viability, odontogenic gene and protein expression levels. However, no significant differences were detected between both groups. The novel dual preconditioning protocol surpassed either treatment alone representing a promising approach for odontogenic induction of mesenchymal stem cells. The results highlighted the regenerative potential of preconditioned sEVs as a biological, promising pulp capping material that could open new avenues in the field of regenerative endodontic treatment after being tested in-vivo in experimental animals.

title: Pulsed Dye Laser for Sensory Dysesthesias Associated With Chronic Radiation Dermatitis.
journal: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD

abstract.text: Chronic radiation dermatitis (CRD) is a long-term complication of radiation therapy, typically manifesting as scarred atrophic plaques with telangiectasias. In some cases, patients report persistent sensory dysesthesias such as burning, stinging, and pruritus. These symptoms are underrecognized and likely underreported but can significantly impair quality of life and are often refractory to conventional therapies. Pulsed dye laser (PDL) has demonstrated efficacy in treating CRD-associated telangiectasias, but its role in alleviating sensory symptoms has not been reported. We report 2 breast cancer patients with treatment-resistant CRD and debilitating dysesthesias who experienced substantial symptom improvement following PDL therapy. The first patient presented with a decade-long nonhealing chest wall wound and refractory pruritus. She underwent ten sessions of subpurpuric PDL at 6-week intervals, in combination with advanced wound care, and achieved complete wound healing and sustained relief of pruritus and skin fragility. The second patient presented with a burning erythematous axillary plaque present for three years. She underwent four PDL sessions at five-week intervals and reported her first meaningful reduction in burning immediately after the initial treatment, with nearly complete resolution of dysesthesia by her final session despite persistent telangiectasias. These cases suggest that PDL may offer a novel therapeutic option for CRD-associated dysesthesias, particularly when integrated with multidisciplinary care involving medical dermatology, laser specialists, and wound care. Larger, prospective studies are warranted to clarify PDL efficacy for CRD-related dysesthesias. &nbsp.

title: The efficacy of a fractionated 1064-nm picosecond Nd: YAG laser compared with a pulsed dye laser for postoperative scar prevention: a prospective split-scar study.
first_affiliation: Department of Dermatology, Hallym University Kangnam Sacred Heart Hospital, Seoul, Republic of Korea.

abstract.text: Pulsed dye lasers (PDLs) are commonly used for early postoperative scar modulation, but evidence for fractionated picosecond lasers is limited. This prospective split-scar study compared the efficacy and safety of a fractionated 1064-nm picosecond Nd: YAG laser with PDL in the early treatment of linear postoperative scars. Fourteen adults received the picosecond Nd: YAG laser on one half of each scar and PDL on the other. Treatments were initiated immediately after suture removal on postoperative day 14 (week 0) in all participants and repeated at weeks 4 and 8. Outcomes were assessed at weeks 0, 4, 8, and 16 using the Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS), Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale-Observer (POSAS-O), and Manchester Scar Scale (MSS). Patient satisfaction was recorded at week 16. Both treatments significantly improved scar appearance by week 16. The fractionated picosecond Nd: YAG laser showed significant reductions in VSS, POSAS-O, and MSS scores, while PDL produced similar improvements. No significant differences were found between treatments over time, and statistical testing confirmed equivalence at week 16 across all scales. Patient satisfaction scores were comparable, and no serious adverse events occurred. Overall, the fractionated 1064-nm picosecond Nd: YAG laser produced short-term postoperative scar outcomes statistically equivalent to those observed with PDL, with good tolerability.

title: A comparative study of the efficacy of apitoxin gel versus photobiomodulation by diode laser for recurrent aphthous stomatitis treatment.
journal: Journal of Taibah University Medical Sciences
first_affiliation: Department of Preventive Dental Sciences, College of Dentistry, Taibah University, Al-Madinah Al-Munawwarah, KSA.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Bee venom (apitoxin) contains bioactive compounds. Diode laser irradiation has a photobiomodulation effect. Both modalities are considered potential alternative therapies for managing recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS).

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study compared the therapeutic effectiveness and safety of apitoxin gel versus photobiomodulation therapy (PBM) for the management of recurrent aphthous ulcers.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Sixty participants with symptomatic recurrent aphthous ulcer ≥4 mm were randomly allocated to two groups. Group I was managed by PBM and group II by using 0.3% apitoxin gel. The pain sensation score measured using a visual analog scale (VAS), and the ulcer surface area and ulcer depth were recorded at baseline and on day 5. The effectiveness index (EI) for pain improvement was calculated for each patient.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The Shapiro-Wilk test was applied to verify the normality of distributions using IBM SPSS software package version 24.0. The independent-samples t-test was used to compare differences between two means. Significant improvements in all clinical parameters were found post-treatment in both study groups compared with the baseline (paired t-test, P < 0.001). According to the intergroup comparison, the clinical improvement was greater in group II, and significant differences in pain sensation (VAS), the EI for pain reduction, and ulcer depth were found between the two groups (independent-samples t-test, P < 0.001). The ulcer surface area did not differ significantly between the two groups post-treatment (independent-samples t-test, P = 0.21).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Apitoxin gel reduces pain, speeds healing, and controls inflammation in RAS. Its effects are due to anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activities, and it may provide a more cost-effective and convenient option for patients.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov, TRN: NCT07135609.

title: The clinical applications of platelet-rich plasma and platelet-rich fibrin combined with photobiomodulation in regenerative dentistry: A literature review.
first_affiliation: Dental Research Center, Dentistry Research Institute, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran.

abstract.text: Regenerative dentistry seeks to restore oral tissues through biologically driven therapies that stimulate endogenous healing. Among these, autologous platelet concentrates-namely platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and platelet-rich fibrin (PRF)-serve as reservoirs of growth factors such as platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF), transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), and insulin-like growth factor (IGF), which promote angiogenesis, cell proliferation, and extracellular matrix formation. Complementing these biological mediators, photobiomodulation (PBM) represents a non-invasive light-based therapy that enhances mitochondrial activity, modulates inflammation, and accelerates tissue regeneration. Accumulating evidence suggests that combining PRP or PRF with PBM produces synergistic effects that surpass those achieved by either modality alone. Experimental and clinical studies demonstrate enhanced angiogenesis, osteogenesis, and wound healing, supported by improved cellular metabolism, growth factor bioavailability, and fibrin architecture. The combined PRP/PRF-PBM approach has shown clinical efficacy across multiple regenerative contexts, including periodontal regeneration, dental implantology, socket preservation, regenerative endodontics, and the management of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw. Additionally, PRP and PRF exhibit antimicrobial effects against key oral pathogens, further reinforcing their therapeutic value. Despite promising results, outcome variability due to differences in preparation methods and PBM parameters highlights the need for standardization and rigorous clinical validation. As understanding deepens, integrating platelet concentrates with PBM may become a cornerstone of evidence-based regenerative dentistry, offering a comprehensive strategy that unites antimicrobial action with enhanced tissue repair.

title: Intense pulsed light as a multi-target intervention paradigm for refractory ocular surface diseases: a review.
first_affiliation: National Clinical Research Center for Ocular Diseases, Eye Hospital, Wenzhou Medical University, Wenzhou, 325027, China.

abstract.text: Ocular surface diseases (OSDs) are a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by overlapping inflammatory, vascular, microbial, neuroimmune, and meibomian gland abnormalities that contribute to the onset and persistence of ocular surface symptoms and signs. Conventional symptom-directed therapies do not adequately alleviate refractory meibomian gland dysfunction, Demodex-associated blepharitis, ocular rosacea, recurrent chalazion, and allergic conjunctivitis. Recent evidence suggests that these conditions may share convergent pathological features, including chronic inflammation, abnormal lid-margin vascularity, and microbial or parasitic imbalance. Intense pulsed light (IPL), which was initially used for vascular and inflammatory disorders in dermatology, has emerged as a potential physical therapy that acts through several proposed mechanisms in patients with selected refractory OSDs, including photothermal liquefaction of inspissated meibum, coagulation of abnormal vessels, reduction of Demodex and microbial burden, modulation of inflammatory responses, and possible effects on neuroimmune signaling; however, these mechanisms remain incompletely established. Case series and clinical studies have reported improvements in ocular symptoms, tear film stability, meibomian gland function and drainage, lid-margin inflammation, and chalazion or lesion resolution, particularly when IPL is combined with meibomian gland expression or other adjunctive therapies. However, treatment responses vary across disease phenotypes and standardized treatment parameters, long-term safety data, and high-quality randomized controlled trials remain limited. Anatomical factors, disease severity, glandular structure, and inflammatory status may also influence therapeutic outcomes. Overall, IPL therapy represents a promising but evolving treatment strategy for refractory OSDs. This review summarizes the current knowledge regarding the proposed mechanisms, clinical applications, treatment protocols, limitations, and future directions and provides updated perspectives for the rational use of IPL in OSD management.

title: Voxel-based ray-tracing modeling of 635 nm optical energy deposition in skin with different pigmentation levels.
first_affiliation: Laser Physics Department, College of Science for Women, University of Babylon, Hillah, Iraq.

abstract.text: Background.Energy absorption in the skin caused by photobiomodulation therapy is highly dependent on the presence of epidermal melanin pigmentation. Accurate determination of the spatial energy distribution is vital for dosimetric purposes based on pigmentation.Methods.A voxel-based numerical model that utilizes the ASAP software package was created to model light scattering and absorption in the skin, comprised of a three-layer system (stratum corneum, epidermis, dermis). The absorbed power density (W mm3) was determined from the voxel-based absorbed energy for an input laser power of 2-20 MW at a wavelength of 635 nm. Low and high pigmentation models were considered using epidermal absorption coefficients selected to represent conditions associated with Fitzpatrick skin types I-II and V-VI, respectively.Results.Power density was shown to have pronounced depth dependence, with maximum power absorption observed at a depth of about 0.02-0.04 mm in the basal epidermis. High pigmentation was accompanied by higher absorption within the superficial epidermal region, with the increased absorption remaining concentrated near the epidermis. The energy-balance check showed agreement between total absorbed and incident power within 5%-8% under the modeled conditions.Conclusion.Skin pigmentation considerably affects spatial power deposition in 635 nm irradiation. The proposed approach represents a physically consistent framework to study effects related to skin pigmentation in optical dosimetry, while its physiological implications need experimental verification.

title: Photobiomodulation Treatment Parameters and Clinical Outcomes Following Periodontal Soft-Tissue Surgery: A Systematic Review.
first_affiliation: Department of Periodontics, Teerthanker Mahaveer Dental College and Research Centre, Teerthanker Mahaveer University, Moradabad, IND.

abstract.text: Photobiomodulation (PBM) has been increasingly investigated as an adjunctive approach to improve postoperative recovery following periodontal surgery. However, substantial variations in treatment parameters and clinical protocols have made it difficult to determine which PBM characteristics are associated with favorable clinical outcomes. This systematic review evaluated the PBM parameters used after periodontal surgery and summarized their reported associations with postoperative clinical outcomes. Randomized controlled clinical studies evaluating PBM after periodontal surgery were identified through a systematic literature search. Studies assessing postoperative pain, wound healing, epithelialization, wound area, graft-related outcomes, and other clinical or biological outcomes were included in this review. Due to substantial heterogeneity in surgical procedures, PBM parameters, application techniques, treatment schedules, and outcome assessments, a quantitative meta-analysis was not performed. Sixteen studies published between 1993 and 2026 were included in this review. Wavelengths ranged from 660 to 970 nm, while power, fluence, application mode, treatment duration, and treatment frequency varied considerably. Overall, PBM has demonstrated potentially favorable effects on wound healing, epithelialization, wound area reduction, and postoperative pain in several studies, although the findings were inconsistent. Some studies have reported no significant improvement in pain or healing despite PBM application. The incomplete reporting of treatment parameters and methodological limitations further restricted the comparison between protocols. Therefore, the available evidence does not establish a specific wavelength, dose, or treatment schedule as optimal. PBM may be a useful adjunct for postoperative periodontal care; however, standardized protocols and adequately powered randomized controlled trials with comprehensive dosimetric reporting are required.

title: Single-component white-light-emitting carbon quantum dots from lignite coal with adaptive broad colour-temperature tunability.
first_affiliation: Environment, Emission and CRM Section, CSIR-Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research Dhanbad Jharkhand 828108 India vikku.010@gmail.com vikram.singh25@csir.res.in.

abstract.text: Sustainable single-component white light emitters exhibiting tunable correlated colour temperature (CCT) while maintaining a nearly constant colour rendering index (CRI) (>75) are very scarce in the literature. In this connection, single-component white-emitting carbon quantum dots (CQDs) were synthesized from Indian lignite coal via a simple one-step dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO)-assisted ultrasonication process at room temperature. The resulting 4.0 nm average-sized CQDs exhibited a broadband emission profile from 400-750 nm across the entire visible spectrum under 390 nm excitation. Remarkably, the CCT can be tuned over a wide range from near warm-white (4535 K) to daylight-white (11 258 K), simply by varying the amount of lignite precursor from 0.03 to 0.08 g, while maintaining the CRI within 74-80. The optimized CQDs displayed chromaticity coordinates of (0.27, 0.34), a CCT of 8612 K, and a CRI of 76. Furthermore, flexible CQD-mixed with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) composite films and CQD-coated light-emitting diode (LED) chips were fabricated, demonstrating their practical utility in solid-state white-light-emitting devices. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of lignite-derived single-component white-emitting CQDs exhibiting controllable broad CCT tunability through simple precursor-mass modulation while preserving acceptable colour-rendering performance.

title: Blue-Light Photobiomodulation in Pediatric Burns: Inflammation, Healing, and Early Scar Outcomes in a Retrospective Historical Cohort.
first_affiliation: Health Professions Department, Meyer Children's Hospital IRCCS, 50139 Florence, Italy.

abstract.text: Background: Blue-light photobiomodulation (PBM) may support burn wound repair through modulation of early inflammatory responses, but comparative evidence in children remains limited. We examined associations between adjunctive PBM, early local inflammation, wound healing, and early scar quality in pediatric burns. Methods: This single-center retrospective historical cohort study included 84 children treated in 2024: 50 historical controls receiving standard care and 34 patients receiving standard care plus blue-light PBM after its introduction into routine practice. The primary outcome was the exploratory composite inflammation score at 72 h, adjusted for the pre-exposure 24 h score and clinical covariates. Secondary outcomes included time to complete re-epithelialization, Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS) score approximately three months after complete re-epithelialization, unplanned dressing changes, and autologous skin grafting. Documented PBM-related adverse events were also reviewed. Results: PBM was associated with a lower adjusted 72 h inflammation score (mean difference -2.70 points, 95% CI -3.71 to -1.68), shorter healing time (-5.98 days, 95% CI -8.68 to -3.28), and lower VSS scores (-1.46 points, 95% CI -2.46 to -0.47). The adjusted odds of unplanned dressing changes were lower with PBM (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.07-0.79), whereas the association with skin grafting was not statistically significant (OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.17-2.16). No PBM-attributable adverse events were documented. Conclusions: These hypothesis-generating associations require prospective confirmation and do not establish a causal treatment effect. The sample size and retrospective recording limit conclusions about safety.

title: Skin thermal damage as an independent pathophysiological entity: Molecular mechanisms distinct from photoaging and implications for systemic conditioning strategies.
first_affiliation: Institute of Information on Traditional Chinese Medicine, China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences, Beijing, 100700, China. Electronic address: huiting2024@163.com.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: While photochemical damage mechanisms have been extensively characterized, thermal damage from infrared (IR) radiation and environmental heat persists as an underappreciated pathophysiological entity. Current photoprotection standards focus exclusively on ultraviolet (UV) blocking, leaving skin vulnerable to thermally-induced aging and systemic deterioration.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To systematically delineate skin thermal damage as distinct from photoaging through comparative molecular energetics analysis, propose an operational scientific definition, and elucidate the paradigm shift from "photon blocking" to "systemic conditioning" for effective thermal protection.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Comprehensive literature synthesis (2022-2025) focusing on epigenetic aging studies, TRPV1 thermosensory mechanisms, heat shock protein dynamics, and multi-targeted pharmacological interventions.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thermal damage operates through physical energy accumulation (molecular vibrational excitation) rather than photochemical bond cleavage, with TRPV1/Ca2+/HSF1 signaling constituting a pathway independent of UV-induced DNA damage. Recent evidence demonstrates that chronic heat exposure accelerates epigenetic aging by 14 months-equivalent to smoking effects (Choi 2025)-through DNAmAge acceleration. Notably, IR effects exhibit dose-dependent biphasicity: low-dose photobiomodulation (<10 J/cm2) confers beneficial preconditioning via mild HSP induction, whereas high-dose thermal accumulation (>42°C tissue temperature) triggers destructive protein denaturation and MMP-1 upregulation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Skin thermal damage represents a "physical dissolution" process characterized by cumulative internal structural disruption, necessitating protection strategies fundamentally different from UV blocking. Traditional Chinese Medicine offers unique advantages through multi-targeted "conditioning" of cellular resilience mechanisms, aligning with the holistic requirements of thermal protection.

title: Effectiveness of a novel low-level laser therapy protocol in managing breast cancer-related lymphedema.
first_affiliation: Pusan National University School of Medicine and Biomedical Research Institute, Pusan National University Hospital, Pusan National University Hospital, Busan, Korea, Republic of.

abstract.text: In this study, we investigate the effects of low-level laser therapy (LLLT) at different wavelengths on lymphedema to further determine the appropriate protocol and effectiveness of LLLT in patients with breast cancer-related lymphedema (BCRL). A randomized controlled trial was conducted involving 46 patients with BCRL. Participants were assigned to receive 904 nm LLLT, 650 nm LLLT, or sham treatment. ICG lymphography was used to assess dermal backflow as a marker of lymphatic dysfunction. Ultrasonography was used to assess subcutaneous thickness and tissue mechanical properties; shear wave velocity (SWV), with higher values indicating greater tissue stiffness, was measured using shear wave elastography. Extracellular fluid volume and local tissue water content were evaluated using multifrequency bioelectrical impedance analysis (MFBIA) and tissue dielectric constant (TDC), respectively. No significant between-group differences were observed in ICG lymphography, MFBIA, or TDC outcomes. For ultrasonographic outcomes, the overall between-group difference in the change in upper-lateral SWV ratio was significant (p = 0.029), and Bonferroni-adjusted post-hoc analysis showed a greater reduction in Group A (904 nm) than in Group B (650 nm) (adjusted p = 0.026). Within Group A, SWV ratios decreased significantly at the lower-lateral site and at the LLLT treatment site. These site-specific findings were not accompanied by measurable changes in lymphatic transport or fluid-related outcomes. Adding 904 nm-650 nm LLLT to conventional decongestive therapy did not produce significant additional effects on extracellular fluid-related or lymphatic functional outcomes. Site-specific reductions in SWV observed with 904 nm LLLT suggest a potential wavelength-dependent effect on local tissue mechanical properties; however, these findings are limited and should be considered exploratory. Larger adequately powered studies with prespecified primary outcomes and longer follow-up are required.

title: Photobiomodulation Irradiation Protocols for Burning Mouth Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Protocol-Level Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
first_affiliation: Department of Oral Medicine, Dental and Life Science Institute, School of Dentistry, Pusan National University, Yangsan-si, Republic of Korea.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the effects of photobiomodulation therapy/low-level laser therapy (PBMT/LLLT) on burning mouth syndrome (BMS) and to explore whether irradiation protocol variables modify treatment effects.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Randomized controlled trials were synthesized according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) and Cochrane guidance. The protocol was registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (CRD420261329136). Random-effects meta-analyses evaluated pain, Oral Health Impact Profile-14 (OHIP-14), xerostomia, anxiety, and depression. Irradiation-related subgroup analyses, including wavelength, power, fluence, irradiation time, session frequency, treatment duration, and application mode, were exploratory.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eighteen trials were included. PBMT/LLLT reduced pain (mean difference [MD] -1.09, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -1.60 to -0.57; I2 = 89%) and improved OHIP-14 (MD -3.82, 95% CI: -4.79 to -2.86; I2 = 41%). Xerostomia and depression were not significantly improved, whereas anxiety showed a modest reduction. Several irradiation protocol variables showed nominal exploratory signals.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: PBMT/LLLT may reduce BMS-related pain and improve oral-health-related quality of life. Current evidence supports irradiation protocol standardization but remains insufficient to define an optimal protocol.

title: Laser Therapy for Cutaneous Vascular Anomalies: Efficacy, Safety, and Innovations.
first_affiliation: Laser and Skin Surgery Center of Indiana, Indianapolis, IN, USA. mj0192@hotmail.com.

abstract.text: Cutaneous vascular anomalies comprise a heterogeneous spectrum of congenital or early-onset vascular lesions, including capillary, venous, lymphatic, and arteriovenous malformations, as well as selected vascular tumors such as infantile hemangiomas. Aberrant vascular development frequently produces conspicuous lesions with attendant psychosocial, cosmetic, and sometimes functional burden. Over the past several decades, laser- and light-based interventions have become fundamental to management, with progressive refinements yielding notable gains in both efficacy and safety. This narrative review evaluates the clinical performance, safety profile, and recent technological advances of laser therapies for cutaneous vascular anomalies, with particular attention to pulsed dye laser (PDL), neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet (Nd:YAG) lasers, intense pulsed light (IPL), and selected emerging platforms including potassium titanyl phosphate (KTP) lasers and multimodal strategies. Relevant literature was reviewed with emphasis on efficacy by lesion subtype, patient selection, peri-procedural planning, post-treatment care, and complication mitigation. PDL remains the reference modality for many superficial vascular lesions, including port-wine stains and superficial infantile hemangiomas, whereas Nd:YAG lasers offer superior penetration for deeper or bulkier lesions at the cost of greater discomfort and a narrower safety margin. IPL and KTP devices provide additional versatility, particularly for superficial telangiectatic and erythematous lesions. Emerging strategies-including dual-wavelength regimens, next-generation large-spot devices, and adjunctive approaches for treatment-resistant lesions-continue to expand the therapeutic armamentarium. When tailored to lesion morphology, skin phototype, patient age, and anatomic site, laser therapy remains a safe and effective cornerstone in the management of cutaneous vascular anomalies. Ongoing innovation and more personalized treatment algorithms are expected to further improve durability of clearance, reduce recurrence, and refine long-term outcomes.

title: Photoacoustic imaging-based assessment of vascular changes in scars: a retrospective analysis of factors influencing PDL treatment efficacy.
first_affiliation: Department of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital, School of Medicine, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, 639 Zhizaoju Rd, 200011, Shanghai, China.

abstract.text: Pulsed dye laser (PDL) is widely used for hypervascular scars, but real-time evaluation of vascular responses remains limited. Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) enables noninvasive, high-resolution assessment of skin microvasculature. To assess whether PAI can visualize post-PDL vascular changes in real time and identify factors influencing efficacy. This single-center retrospective study analyzed 32 scars treated with 595-nm PDL. Patients were grouped by pulse duration/fluence combination (0.45-6.0 J/cm², 1.5-8.0 J/cm², or 3.0-10.0 J/cm²) or by endpoint (purpuric or nonpurpuric response). PAI, Antera 3D, and Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS) assessments were performed at baseline, immediately after treatment, and 1 month later. PAI enabled real-time, layer-specific visualization of vascular change, a capability that is less readily achievable with the VSS or Antera 3D. No statistically detectable association was identified between the parameter combinations and PDL outcomes. By contrast, the treatment endpoint was significantly associated with vascular outcomes: compared with purpuric treatment, nonpurpuric treatment showed lower adjusted full-dermis vessel density (30.25% vs. 49.29%; difference, - 19.04%; 95% CI, - 28.12 to - 9.97; Holm-adjusted P < 0.001) and smaller vessel diameter (278.74 μm vs. 428.36 μm; ratio, 0.651; 95% CI, 0.500-0.846; Holm-adjusted P = 0.002). Layer-specific outcomes also showed a similar direction of effect. In the exploratory repeated-treatment subset, NPUR was associated with progressive vascular improvement. PAI helps characterize vascular features and may provide additional information to support overall treatment parameter selection. Treatment endpoint was significant correlated to vascular efficacy. PAI suggests that vascular closure without purpura maybe potentially favorable.

title: Can photobiomodulation prevent herpes labialis recurrences? A systematic review.
first_affiliation: Faculdade Israelita de Ciências da Saúde Albert Einstein, Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein, São Paulo, SP, Brazil.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness of photobiomodulation for preventing recurrent herpes labialis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Eligibility criteria were defined using the PICOS framework, and only randomized clinical trials were included. We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, the Virtual Health Library, and gray-literature sources. Of the records identified, nine reports underwent full-text assessment, and three studies met the eligibility criteria.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Two trials reported lower recurrence frequencies after photobiomodulation compared to control interventions, while one trial found no difference. Findings regarding recurrence severity and duration were inconsistent across studies. No adverse events were reported in the studies that provided safety data.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The available evidence suggests that photobiomodulation may reduce the recurrence frequency, severity, and duration of herpes labialis. However, the certainty of the evidence was rated as low due to small sample sizes, incomplete blinding, and variations in laser parameters and comparators. These limitations restrict generalizability and preclude definitive clinical recommendations. Well-designed randomized controlled trials with standardized protocols and consistent outcome measures are needed to establish the clinical utility of photobiomodulation for recurrent herpes labialis.

title: The importance of power in photobiomodulation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of high-intensity laser therapy.
first_affiliation: Personalized Health Research Services, LLC, Winter Park, FL, United States.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Low-level laser therapy (LLLT; ≤ 0.5 W) is guideline-recommended in the United States for shallow-tissue oral mucositis and other superficial pathologies but has generally failed in trials for deeper tissue conditions due to limited penetration and subtherapeutic dosing. By contrast, Class IV high-intensity laser therapy (HILT; ≥ 0.5-80 W), typically at ∼100-fold higher power, has proven successful for many of these deeper tissue indications.

abstract.label: METHODS
